entry.title: Add comparison to BIP-118 in BIP-448
entry.summary:
The discussion primarily revolves around the concerns and considerations associated with implementing changes in Bitcoin Improvement Proposals (BIPs), specifically those related to softforks. There is a particular focus on the concept of the "risk surface" which is a crucial factor to consider when evaluating any BIP associated with softforks. The risk surface refers to the potential vulnerabilities or problems that could arise from implementing the proposal, suggesting that this should always be at the forefront of considerations.
Additionally, the conversation touches on specific opcodes like CAT, highlighting its unique characteristics even though it serves similar functions to others within its category. This specificity in referencing opcodes underlines the nuanced approach needed when integrating new features into the blockchain protocol. Furthermore, the mention of APO as significant suggests that some elements within these proposals warrant particular attention due to their impact or functionality within the system.
This email underscores the intricacy and careful consideration required in the development and review of Bitcoin Improvement Proposals. Each element, from general concepts like the risk surface to specific opcodes, plays a critical role in the broader context of blockchain technology’s evolution and security.
